From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>

Subject: Intro call recap — SDK / auth / routing & tool-calling patterns (next steps)

Hi Emma — great to meet earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so we can scope the technical deep dive.

Call highlights (what I heard):
- You want an embeddable SDK path for server-side inference within an existing VPC (on-prem adjacent).
- Primary auth is Okta SSO + SCIM for user provisioning; infra team prefers KMS for key control.
- Use case: document ingestion -> embedding retrieval -> re-ranker -> structured tool calls to 3rd-party data services (credit check, ledger lookup).
- Latency target for user-facing flows: 300–500ms median for a single-turn retrieval + rerank + tool enrichment; background batch tasks can be slower.

Questions from our side to prep the deep dive:
1) Can you confirm whether the production plan is Private (VPC) or a Dedicated tenancy?
2) Are there network egress restrictions (IP allowlist / proxy) or strict egress blocking?
3) Size/shape of retrieval corpus (documents, average tokens) and expected QPS for peak flows.
4) Any compliance artifacts we should prep ahead (SOC 2 evidence, penetration-test reports)?

Suggested integration patterns we'll propose in the technical deep dive:
- SDK setup: server-side Node/Python SDK with explicit connection modes (hosted API vs Private tunnel).
- Auth: Okta OIDC for user flows + customer-managed KMS for secret wrapping if on Private.
- Routing: policy-based routing by latency vs cost; fallback to smaller quantized model if high-cost/burst scenario.
- Tool calling: define typed tool schemas (JSON Schema), use parallel enrichment for non-blocking tools, enforce timeouts + graceful fallback to cached responses.
- Embeddings + reranker: retrieval via embeddings store (ann index), top-N candidates followed by reranker model for final ordering.

Attachments: redwood-integration-one-pager.pdf (integration summary), mutual-action-plan.xlsx (starter MAP).

Next steps:
- Can you confirm answers to the questions above?
- If OK, propose a 90-min technical deep dive next week with your infra lead and Okta admin.

Thanks — I’ll loop in Marissa (SE) and Diego (Solutions) to own the technical agenda.

— Sean
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference

Subject: Fwd: Intro call recap — initial technical notes + recommended patterns

Folks — forwarding Emma's answers. Below are our recommended patterns to validate on the call. These are deliberately pragmatic so we can scope work and identify open action items.

1) Tool definition & contract
- Each tool (credit-check, ledger-lookup, AML-enrich) gets a typed definition: name, input_schema (JSON Schema), output_schema (JSON Schema), owned_timeout_ms, retry_policy (max_retries, backoff_ms), side_effects (bool).
- Tool responses must be validated against output_schema; failures trigger fallback (cached value or quick summary).

2) Tool choice & orchestration patterns
- Synchronous critical: credit-check -> call in the main path with 300–500ms target; mark as blocking.
- Parallel non-critical: ledger-lookup & enrichment called in parallel and merged when available; provide partial UI state while waiting.
- Circuit breaker: configure per-tool CB with short window to avoid cascading latency.

3) Error handling & graceful degradation
- Fail-fast for blocking tools with clear user messaging; for enrichment tools, allow partial answers and schedule background reconciliation.
- Instrumentation: per-tool latency histograms and error rates in Redwood Console; automatic fallback to cached embeddings / older model if reranker fails.

4) Embedding + re-ranker flow
- Retrieval: ANN index returns top-50 candidates (fast), do client-side lightweight filter then send top-8 to the re-ranker model.
- Re-ranker: use a smaller, faster cross-encoder tuned on your prompt sets; return structured scores for deterministic selection.

5) SDK & auth setup
- Provide server-side SDK samples for node/python with patterns: connection_mode = {"private_tunnel","direct_api"}, auth = {"okta_oidc","service_jwt"}.
- KMS integration: support encrypt/decrypt hooks so keys never leave Finlytics KMS.

6) Observability & compliance
- Capture token-level cost/lifetime, per-request trace id, and attach to audit logs exported to your SIEM.

Open action items to validate on the call:
- Confirm static IP/peering option for Private nodes.
- Identify which downstream tools are blocking vs async.
- Validate sample doc subset for embedding size and reranker tuning.

I attached a one-pager and starter MAP. I recommend we lock agenda: 1) Network & auth (20 min), 2) Tool catalog & patterns (30 min), 3) Embedding/re-ranker design (25 min), 4) Action items & owners (15 min).

— Sean

Attachments referenced: redwood-integration-one-pager.pdf, mutual-action-plan.xlsx
